provenance: legacy SemStreams capture; not a SemEngine result

verdicts.rationale: runSourceMenu obtains registered SourceWizard implementations and consumes their availability, type keys, labels, and prompts. The interface defines the contract that drives this initialization menu.

wizard_url.go's init directly registers urlWizard through RegisterSourceWizard, following the registration function's documented initialization convention. The pair shows how this source type enters the shared wizard registry.

gitWizard.Prompts directly uses resolvableGitURL for its default and normalizes user-supplied local paths. Both implement the requirement that git source identity use a resolvable remote or absolute path rather than a bare dot.

buildDetectedSources reads ProjectInfo fields to build git, AST, documentation, config, and image entries. The detected-facts type and its quick-setup consumer jointly define this configuration derivation.

DetectProject stores deriveNamespace's result in info.Namespace, which Init uses as the prompt default and validates before constructing the config. The pair supplies derivation and user acceptance of the same namespace.

parseVideoFlags and videoWizard.Prompts both populate the video source settings and matching default interval, size, and watch behavior. Their differing scene-threshold handling makes co-inspection useful for maintaining the two interfaces to one source contract.

Both functions infer a language from manifest filenames, feeding different setup entry points. DetectProject's additional Python manifests expose a real difference within the shared language-detection responsibility.
Remove directly calls sourceLocation to label the source being selected for deletion. Its fallback for an empty location depends on the formatter's type-specific result.
audioWizard.Available directly calls ffmpegAvailable and reports the missing executable when the probe fails. The helper in the video file also determines audio wizard availability.
Add reads Wizards(), displays their availability and descriptions, and invokes the selected wizard's Prompts. The accessor's registry contents determine the interactive add menu and its behavior.

cfgWizard.Prompts selects project manifest files as ingestion data, whereas buildConfig constructs semsource's own namespace/source configuration. The overloaded config term refers to source content in one case and service setup in the other.

printSummary reports a newly written setup config and provides startup guidance; Validate loads an existing config and reports validation. Their repeated namespace and source-count output does not establish one command responsibility.

Term.Select implements reusable single-choice input, while runSourceMenu owns an initialization-specific multi-toggle selection loop. Their numbered-menu parsing scaffold masks distinct selection contracts and neither entity calls the other.

Remove selects and deletes an existing source entry before persisting it; writeAndSummarize completes initial setup and prints guidance. Shared JSON/file-writing boilerplate does not make their command responsibilities interchangeable.

addNonInteractive dispatches explicit source arguments to flag parsers, whereas shouldPreselect computes initial menu selections from detection facts. They share type-key cases but answer dispatch and default-selection questions separately.

detectGitRemote retrieves the origin URL for git defaults and namespace derivation; ffmpegAvailable tests media-tool availability. Their exec-package usage is a shared mechanism serving different source responsibilities.

joinPaths formats detected paths for presentation, while splitComma parses flag input into path or URL values. Their comma-list resemblance does not make hint rendering and noninteractive input parsing one workflow.

orgFromRemote extracts an organization for namespace identity, while gitWizard.Prompts uses URL shape to normalize local source paths. Similar remote syntax checks implement namespace selection and git source-location handling separately.

detectLanguage maps manifests to a language; detectConfigFiles returns files to ingest as config content. The overlapping os.Stat probes and filenames serve distinct questions about code language and ingestion paths.

repoWizard configures an all-in-one clone for code, docs, and config; gitWizard configures commit-history ingestion. Their matching URL/branch/watch fields obscure different source types, which the wizard labels and preselection comment explicitly distinguish.
